prompt: A new terminal answers `aws sts get-caller-identity` with `InvalidClientTokenId`. What happened?
hint: Who refuses a key made of the word test?

choices.text: moto rejected the key pair
choices.why: moto accepts any credentials at all; it never answers with this error.

choices.text: moto is not running in the other terminal
choices.why: A stopped moto gives a connection error on localhost:4567, not a refused token.

choices.text: The region sa-east-1 does not exist in moto
choices.why: moto answers in sa-east-1; the transcripts were all recorded there.

choices.text: It reached the real AWS, which refuses the key
choices.why: Right. Without AWS_ENDPOINT_URL in that terminal the command line calls AWS, and AWS refuses the test key.

prompt: You stopped moto last night and start it again this morning. What is still there from yesterday's practice?
hint: Where does moto keep what it is told?

choices.text: Nothing: moto kept it all in memory
choices.why: Right. moto forgets everything when it stops, which is why each lesson builds what it needs.

choices.text: Everything, saved in ~/aws/venv
choices.why: The virtual environment holds moto's program, not its data.

choices.text: The buckets, but not the other resources
choices.why: No service is kept: S3 in moto lives in the same memory as the rest.

choices.text: Whatever the AWS account synchronised overnight
choices.why: There is no AWS account in this course for anything to come from.

prompt: A call to `kms:Decrypt` succeeds against moto with a user whose policy should deny it. What does that prove?
hint: What does moto check by default?

choices.text: That the policy is written correctly
choices.why: moto did not read the policy at all; a wrong policy would have passed too.

choices.text: That AWS would allow the same call
choices.why: By default moto evaluates no IAM policy, so its answer says nothing about AWS's.

choices.text: That the key is not scheduled for deletion
choices.why: moto decrypts with a key pending deletion too; the course shows it.

choices.text: Only that the request was well formed
choices.why: Right. moto accepted the shape of the request; permission was never checked.

prompt: Which of these does moto 5.2.3 actually do? Choose all that apply.
hint: Storing and answering, yes; doing the work behind the answer, mostly no.

choices.text: Return the average of the data points you stored
choices.why: Yes. Sums, averages, minima and maxima come back computed.

choices.text: Move an alarm to ALARM when its metric crosses the threshold
choices.why: No. moto never evaluates an alarm; its state changes only when you set it.

choices.text: Create a stack from a CloudFormation template
choices.why: Yes. Creating and deleting stacks works; change sets on updates and drift do not.

choices.text: Run the commands of a buildspec
choices.why: No. A build is marked successful with invented durations and nothing runs.

choices.text: Report the price of a resource
choices.why: No. moto has no prices; they come from AWS's public price list.

prompt: You decide to open a real AWS account to compare. What comes first, before anything is created?
hint: Two protections, in a fixed order.

choices.text: Create an access key for the root user and save it in ~/aws
choices.why: A root access key is the most dangerous credential an account has, and no file of this course should hold a real key.

choices.text: A second factor on the root user, then a budget with an alert
choices.why: Right. Protect the root user, then make sure a bill cannot grow unseen.

choices.text: Point AWS_ENDPOINT_URL at the account
choices.why: That variable is what sends requests to moto; with a real account you leave it unset.

choices.text: Turn on the free tier so nothing is billed
choices.why: The free tier is no switch and no promise: a forgotten resource is billed anyway.

prompt: A build runs 8 minutes on `build.general1.small` in São Paulo, at the list price of 0.005 USD a minute. The pipeline runs it 300 times in a month. What do the builds cost, before the free minutes?
In a line printed by `price.py`, what is `SAE1-Build-Min:Linux:g1.small`?
hint: It is the name a bill uses.

choices.text: The usage type, named as on a bill
choices.why: Right. The usage type is how the bill and the price list name the same line; SAE1 is São Paulo.

choices.text: The build project's name in CodeBuild
choices.why: The project is yours to name; this string is AWS's and the same for every account.

choices.text: The image the build container runs
choices.why: The image is aws/codebuild/standard:7.0 in the project; this names a machine size and its price.

choices.text: The offer version the price was read from
choices.why: The version is pinned inside price.py, and its date is printed in the first line.

prompt: The build writes `report.html` next to `imagedefinitions.json`, but only lists the second under `artifacts`. Can the deploy action read `report.html`?

choices.text: Yes, because both actions share the build's container
choices.why: Each action runs on its own; the build's container is gone when the build ends.

choices.text: Yes, if the deploy action runs within an hour of the build
choices.why: Time has nothing to do with it: the file was never put in the bucket.

choices.text: No: only what the build listed is zipped into the bucket and passed on
choices.why: Right. An unlisted file never leaves the build's container.

choices.text: No, because the deploy action can read the registry only
choices.why: The deploy action reads its input artifact from the bucket; the registry holds the image.

prompt: Anyone in the company can open a pull request, and the build runs the repository's own buildspec. Which role is it most important to keep narrow?
hint: Whose code does each role run?

choices.text: The pipeline's role, because it starts everything
choices.why: The pipeline service runs AWS's code, not the repository's; the build runs whatever was committed.

choices.text: The build's, since it runs what was committed
choices.why: Right. A wide build role turns a pull request into a way to act in the account.

choices.text: The deployment's role, because it touches production
choices.why: It matters, but it runs a fixed AWS action; the build runs arbitrary commands.

choices.text: None, as long as the artifact bucket is private
choices.why: A private bucket does not limit what a build's credentials can do elsewhere.

prompt: Match each service to the one job it does in the chain.
hint: One job each, and one job that belongs to none of them.

pairs.right: Knows the order of the steps
Runs commands in a fresh container
Moves traffic to the new version

prompt: `docker build` fails in the `build` phase. The buildspec's `post_build` pushes the image and has no check. What happens next?
hint: Which phase is skipped after a failure in build?

choices.text: The build stops at once and post_build never runs
choices.why: That is what a failure in install or pre_build does; a failure in build still runs post_build.

choices.text: post_build runs and pushes the image
choices.why: Right. post_build runs with CODEBUILD_BUILD_SUCCEEDING set to 0, and without a check it publishes.

choices.text: CodeBuild retries the build phase three times
choices.why: Nothing is retried unless the buildspec asks for it.

choices.text: The pipeline rolls the service back
choices.why: The deploy stage never starts after a failed build; there is nothing to roll back.

prompt: In `post_build`, the variable that is `0` when an earlier command of the build failed is CODEBUILD_BUILD____.
hint: One word, in capitals, after BUILD_.

prompt: moto reports a build with every phase `SUCCEEDED`. What does that tell you about your buildspec?

choices.text: That its tests passed
choices.why: No test ran: there was no source and no tests directory in the lab.

choices.text: That its YAML is valid for CodeBuild
choices.why: moto never opened the file; a broken buildspec gets the same answer.

choices.text: Nothing: moto ran none of it and invented the durations
choices.why: Right. The phases add up to more than the build lasted; no command ran.

choices.text: That docker build works with privilegedMode
choices.why: There is no Docker in moto at all.

prompt: `create-pipeline` fails with *CodePipeline is not authorized to perform AssumeRole on role …/shop-build*. What is the fix?
hint: Who does the role's trust policy name?

choices.text: Give the build's role the AdministratorAccess policy
choices.why: Permissions are not the problem: the pipeline service is not allowed to assume the role at all.

choices.text: Its own role, trusted by CodePipeline
choices.why: Right. The build's role trusts CodeBuild only; the pipeline needs one whose trust policy names codepipeline.amazonaws.com.

choices.text: Run the command again with the root user
choices.why: The caller is not what failed; the service's right to wear the role is.

choices.text: Create the pipeline first and the role afterwards
choices.why: The service checks the role when the pipeline is created, so it has to exist and trust it first.

prompt: Put the stages of the shop's pipeline in the order they run.
hint: Evidence first, people second, production last.
items: Source: the commit is zipped into src
Build: tests run and the image is pushed
Approve: a person approves or rejects
Deploy: ECS runs the image the artifact names
trap: Approval before the build is the slip: a person would approve something nobody has tested yet.

prompt: Five commits land in ten minutes on a pipeline in the default `SUPERSEDED` mode, while an earlier run waits at the manual approval. What reaches the approval?
hint: A waiting run can be replaced.

choices.text: Five runs, queued one behind the other
choices.why: That is QUEUED mode, which a V2 pipeline has to choose.

choices.text: Only the first commit, and the other four are dropped for good
choices.why: It is the older waiting runs that are superseded, not the newer ones.

choices.text: The newest commit, superseding the runs that were waiting
choices.why: Right. A newer run that reaches the same point replaces a waiting older one.

choices.text: Five runs at once, in parallel
choices.why: Runs that do not wait for each other is PARALLEL mode, not the default.

prompt: A V2 pipeline's run has a 5-minute build action and a 3-minute deploy action, and runs 400 times in a month in São Paulo at 0.002 USD per action minute. What do the action minutes cost, after the 100 free minutes?
hint: Total action minutes, less 100, times the price.

prompt: A deploy action needs to know which image to run. Where does it read that from?
hint: The image and the artifact travel separately.

choices.text: From the image itself, which the build put in the artifact bucket
choices.why: The image goes to the registry; the bucket holds a small file naming it.

choices.text: From the latest tag in ECR
choices.why: Deploying whatever latest points at is exactly what lesson 2 argues against.

choices.text: From the pipeline's JSON definition
choices.why: The definition names the file to read, not the image, which changes every run.

choices.text: From imagedefinitions.json, the artifact the build wrote
choices.why: Right. The file names the image URI, and ECS pulls that image from ECR.
